{{Short description|None}}
[[File:Scottybowman-2006awards.jpg|thumb|right|Hall of Famer Scotty Bowman won five Stanley Cup championships while coaching the Canadiens.]]
Officially known as ''le Club de hockey Canadien'',<ref>{{cite web|url=http://canadiens.nhl.com/team/app/?service=page&page=NHLPage&id=16903 |title=Privacy Policy |publisher=Lincoln Hockey and the National Hockey League |work=NHL.com |access-date=2008-12-21 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081216164421/http://canadiens.nhl.com/team/app/?service=page&page=NHLPage&id=16903 |archive-date=2008-12-16 }}</ref> the [[Montreal Canadiens]] ({{langx|fr|Les Canadiens de Montréal}}) are a Canadian professional [[ice hockey]] team based in [[Montreal]], [[Quebec]]. They play in the [[Atlantic Division (NHL)|Atlantic Division]] of the [[Eastern Conference (NHL)|Eastern Conference]] in the [[National Hockey League]] (NHL). In 1909, the Canadiens were founded as a charter member of the [[National Hockey Association]] (NHA). In 1917, the franchise joined the NHL, and is one of the [[Original Six]] teams.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2008/writers/sarah_kwak/10/08/original.six/index.html |title=Original Six in the spotlight |author=Sarah Kwak |publisher=Time Inc |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=2008-10-09 |access-date=2008-12-21 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090123054444/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2008/writers/sarah_kwak/10/08/original.six/index.html |archive-date=2009-01-23 }}</ref> In their 100-year history, the Canadiens have won 24&nbsp;[[Stanley Cup]] [[List of Stanley Cup champions|championships]], and are the last Canadian team to have won the Stanley Cup, having done so in 1993.<ref name="cup"/> Having played in the [[Jubilee Arena]] (1909–1910,1918–1919), the [[Montreal Arena]] (1911–1918), the [[Mount Royal Arena]] (1919–1926), and the [[Montreal Forum]] (1926–1996), the Canadiens have played their home games at the [[Bell Centre]], formerly known as the Molson Centre, since 1996.<ref>{{cite book |title=The Montreal Canadiens |last=Mouton |first=Claude |publisher=Key Porter Books |year=1987|isbn=1-55013-051-X}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.centrebell.ca/en/our_history |title=Our History |publisher=[[Bell Centre|Centre Bell]] |access-date=2008-12-21 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081218103416/http://centrebell.ca/en/our_history |archive-date=2008-12-18 }}</ref> The Canadiens are owned by the [[Molson Family]]. The general manager position is filled by [[Kent Hughes (ice hockey)|Kent Hughes]] while their coaches consist of [[Martin St. Louis]] as their head coach, [[Trevor Letowski]] and [[Stephane Robidas]] as assistant coaches, and Marco Marciano as the interim goaltender coach<ref>{{Cite news |date=2026-01-28 |title=Canadiens fire goaltending coach Eric Raymond |url=https://montrealgazette.com/sports/hockey/montreal-canadiens/canadiens-fire-goaltending-coach-eric-raymond |access-date=2026-01-28 |work=Montreal Gazette}}</ref>. The current captain of the Canadiens is [[Nick Suzuki]].

There have been 28&nbsp;[[head coach]]es for the Canadiens franchise in the NHL. The team's first head coach in the NHL was [[Newsy Lalonde]], who coached the Canadiens for eight NHL seasons in two stints. Although [[Dick Irvin]] coached the team for 15 seasons, [[Toe Blake]], who coached two fewer seasons, is the franchise's all-time leader for the most regular-season games coached (914), the most regular-season games won (500), the most regular-season [[Point (ice hockey)|points]] (1159), the most playoff games coached (119), and the most playoff games won (82). Blake has also won the most Stanley Cup championships with eight; [[Scotty Bowman]] has won five, Irvin has won three, [[Cecil Hart]] has won two, and [[Léo Dandurand|Leo Dandurand]], [[Claude Ruel]], [[Al MacNeil]], [[Jean Perron]], and [[Jacques Demers]] have won one each. Lalonde won a Stanley Cup championship in 1915–16 while in the NHA.<ref name="cup"/> Bowman and [[Pat Burns]] have each been awarded the [[Jack Adams Award]], in 1976–77 and 1988–89 respectively. Nine head coaches have spent their entire NHL head coaching careers with the Canadiens. Bowman and Dandurand have been elected to the [[Hockey Hall of Fame]] as [[List of members of the Hockey Hall of Fame#Builders|builders]]. Dandurand is the only coach to have spent his entire NHL head coaching career with the Canadiens and to have been elected to the Hockey Hall of Fame as a builder.

==Notes==
* {{note label|Note1|a|a}} A running total of the number of coaches of the Canadiens. Thus, any coach who has two or more separate terms as head coach is only counted once.
* {{note label|Note2|b|b}} Before the 2005–06 season, the NHL instituted a [[Overtime (ice hockey)#Shootout|penalty shootout]] for regular season games that remained tied after a five-minute overtime period, which prevented ties.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nhl.com/ext/0708rules.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080511234846/http://www.nhl.com/ext/0708rules.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-date=2008-05-11 |title=Official Rules |publisher=Lincoln Hockey and the National Hockey League |work=NHL.com |access-date=2008-12-21 }}</ref>
* {{note label|Note3|c|c}} In ice hockey, the winning percentage is calculated by dividing points by maximum possible [[Point (ice hockey)|points]].
* {{note label|Note4|d|d}} Each year is linked to an article about that particular NHL season.
* {{note label|Note5|e|e 1}}{{note label|Note5|e|2}}{{note label|Note5|e|3}}{{note label|Note5|e|4}}{{note label|Note5|e|5}}{{note label|Note5|e|6}}{{note label|Note5|e|7}}{{note label|Note5|e|8}}{{note label|Note5|e|9}}{{note label|Note5|e|10}} [[Newsy Lalonde]], [[Babe Siebert]], [[Sylvio Mantha]], [[Dick Irvin]], [[Toe Blake]], [[Bernie Geoffrion]], [[Jacques Lemaire]], [[Jacques Laperrière|Jacques Laperriere]], [[Bob Gainey]], and [[Martin St. Louis]] have been inducted into the [[Hockey Hall of Fame]] as [[List of members of the Hockey Hall of Fame#Players|players]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hockey-reference.com/awards/hhof.html |title=Hockey Hall of Fame Inductees |access-date=2008-12-21 |publisher=Sports Reference LLC |work=Hockey-Reference.com |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081011093831/http://www.hockey-reference.com/awards/hhof.html |archive-date=2008-10-11 }}</ref>
* {{note label|Note6|f|f}} [[Babe Siebert]] was named the head coach for the [[1939–40 NHL season|1939–40 season]], but died from drowning during the off-season.<ref name="siebert"/>
